summary: a park is read off the shape of the commit that wrote it — the entry's note and nothing else — so a park that also touched a file is a ship, and a note's kind lives in its prose
acceptance: a build note that parks its entry lives under `notes/parked/` and an observation beside it does not, the park predicate reads that location rather than the commit's path list, and the records gate holds both directories.
tests: a note under the parked directory parks its entry
a note beside the parked directory ships its entry
a commit writing a parked note and the entry's work is still a park
the records gate refuses a parked note written under another tick's tag
notes: Ruling: location is kind. `isPark` (harness/chain.ts) is the path-list read, and both `namedLinesGate` and `shipped` consume it. The record listing and the plan fence both compose from `RECORD_DIR_NAMES`, so the parked directory joins there rather than at each reader.

summary: the declaration names no findings scripts and the inbox slice runs none, so a consumer's per-tick measurement has no route into the drain the package already runs
acceptance: declared findings scripts run at the tip before the slice renders, the slice stamps the record names it drained and materializes only names it has not seen since the stamp, and those files render and drain exactly as the inbox's do.
tests: a declared findings script's unseen stdout lines are materialized as record files
a findings script re-emitting a stamped record name materializes nothing
the inbox slice renders a materialized findings record beside the inbox's

notes: Wire shape ratified: one `{ name, body }` object per line. The delta is the package's, never the script's — a consumer measuring a standing set re-emits it every tick and pays only its first drain. Watch the records gate: the package writes the materialized file and the slice drains it the same tick. Blocked on the friction leg, which rewrites the same window.

setup.serialize leaves the wave's other provisioning parallel
an undeclared serialize runs restores concurrently
notes: The reduction is `provisioning(api, declaration)` in harness/chain.ts, built once per chain load — so the serialization is that function's own queue, not a second mechanism beside it. The `setup` row of the declaration table already states the behavior.

summary: a bay has no way to say a job is a named fence over shared values, so each job carries a second declaration and a loader the package should own
acceptance: `jobs` maps a job name to a specLocus, a fence and optional slots and capabilities, a chain loaded under a job's state root applies that job's values over the shared declaration — capabilities added to the shared set rather than replacing it — and an absent `jobs` resolves the repo-level one-job case.
tests: a chain loaded under a named job's state root takes that job's specLocus and fence
a named job's slots override the declaration's shared slots
a named job's capabilities add to the declaration's shared set
a declaration naming no jobs resolves the repo-level values
the chain the factory builds declares a seedDir at the package's skeleton
notes: The engine's job partition already gives each job its state root (spec/jobs.md); which job the chain is under is read from api.paths.flumeDir. `flume job new` seeds from the package skeleton through the factory's declared seedDir — harness/ declares none today, so that is part of this entry. Blocked on the shared capabilities field this one adds to.

edit.description: the job-fence refusal at chain load, naming the glob and the root
the refusal, its message, and the admitted consumer file
the refusal arrives at load, not at a tick

summary: nothing refuses a job fence whose globs reach the package's own artifacts under a sibling job's state root, so one job's build writes another job's queue
acceptance: chain load refuses a job fence glob that can match the package's queue, plan state, a record or a note under any state root but the job's own, naming the glob and the root; a consumer's own file under a sibling root still loads.
tests: a job fence reaching the package's queue under a sibling job's root refuses the load
the refusal names the offending glob and the root it reaches
a job fence reaching a consumer's own file under a sibling root loads
notes: The engine declines cross-job fence policing by design (spec/jobs.md) and every package gate keys on the tick's own root, so the refusal is the package's alone. The artifact set is the package's own layout — queue, plan state, records, notes — never a consumer's product; where a bay keeps its product is the bay's.

summary: the default handoff re-dispatches an entry whose latest attempt was a clean exit at the current HEAD — the same dispatch against an unchanged world, for the same outcome
acceptance: the package declares the engine's per-entry refusal, and an entry whose latest prior attempt is a clean exit at the tick's own HEAD is not handed to build while one at an older HEAD still is.
tests: an entry whose latest clean exit is at the current HEAD is not handed to build
an entry whose latest clean exit is at an older HEAD is handed to build
an entry whose latest attempt is a gate revert at the current HEAD is handed to build
notes: Read from the mode and the anchor the engine reports on the record — PriorAttempt's `mode` and `headSha` (src/Prompt.ts) — never a heuristic of the package's own. Only clean-exit qualifies; every other mode describes a world the next tick can change.
